findings.summary: Version-bound review validation and delivery are not synchronized with explicit version activation. finish_goal_call checks the active version before calling _effect_outcome, which performs journal operations before invoking the external approve/reject port. activate_version can persist and activate v2 during that interval, allowing a review naming v1 to reach the port after v2 becomes active. The journal lock protects individual journal operations, not the validation-to-delivery boundary. The existing regression covers activation in an earlier list item, but not this concurrent interleaving. This leaves the concurrency protection requested by the archived Final review unresolved and violates behavior 3's version-bound review guard. Serialize version activation with review-effect admission or provide equivalent atomic version enforcement, and add an offline barrier-controlled regression.

The supplied input_commit and subject_commit are identical full RC identities. The current feedback index and Continuous artifact identify 601781c4aa7c8d155e5312d0b9fab07063580703 as the distinct implementation subject. Mechanical I-to-RC product-tree equivalence was not established with the available file-inspection tools; no shell or Git command was executed and no product-tree mismatch is asserted. Actual Git HEAD verification remains the deterministic seal's responsibility. Several archived JSON records were truncated by the inspection tools, so complete feedback-history verification is not claimed.

Continuous independently records APPROVE with a note about deferred version-activation wiring. Final independently records REJECT for the development-stage synchronization defect above, not for the deferred live binding. The implementation handoff reports compileall exit 0 and 59 passing kernel tests; these are implementation-reported results, not checks executed by this reviewer.

Live Runtime, integration, deployment, real-process stop/resume, actual reply delivery, merge recovery, full Session queries and joint E2E were not run by this reviewer. These remain deferred under the authorized development-stage scope and are not grounds for rejection. This review does not establish production acceptance or whole-Goal ready_for_joint_validation.
